general.sign: Confusion or slurred speech, very fast breathing, or pale, blue or blotchy skin, often with fever or shivering
general.why: These can be signs of sepsis: the body's reaction to an infection has started to damage its own organs.

general.sign: Fainting and not waking up within a minute, or fainting with chest pain, a racing heart or a fit
general.why: This can be a dangerous heart rhythm or a severe allergic reaction.

general.sign: Fever, shivering or feeling very ill in the days after an injection
general.why: Germs from the needle, the skin or the product may have reached your blood. If you also have a fast heartbeat or fast breathing, call your local emergency number.

general.sign: You fainted, but woke up quickly and now feel well
general.why: Fainting is often harmless, but a doctor should check the cause.

general.sign: A new mole, or a mole that changes size, shape or colour, itches or bleeds
general.why: A changing mole can be skin cancer, and tanning peptides such as melanotan II have been linked to new and changing moles in case reports.

injection.sign: Pain at the injection spot that is much worse than it looks, or dark, purple or grey patches or blisters there
injection.why: This can be a rare, fast-spreading infection of the deep layers under the skin (necrotising fasciitis).

injection.sign: Redness, heat, swelling or pain around the injection spot that keeps growing or getting worse
injection.why: This can be a skin infection (cellulitis), which needs antibiotics before it spreads.

injection.sign: Red lines that run from the injection spot towards the armpit or groin
injection.why: The infection may be spreading along the lymph vessels, and from there into the blood. If you also have a fever with a fast heartbeat or fast breathing, call your local emergency number.

injection.sign: A painful, warm lump that fills with pus
injection.why: This is probably an abscess: it often needs draining by a doctor, so do not squeeze it.

injection.sign: You were pricked by a needle that someone else had used
injection.why: Blood on a used needle can pass on HIV and hepatitis B or C, and preventive treatment works best within hours.

injection.sign: A lump at an injection spot that does not go away, or keeps growing
injection.why: A doctor should check whether it is an abscess, a reaction to the product or something else.

allergic.sign: Swelling of the lips, tongue or throat, trouble breathing or swallowing, wheezing, a hoarse voice, or feeling faint, soon after an injection
allergic.why: This can be a severe allergic reaction (anaphylaxis), which is life-threatening and gets worse very quickly.

allergic.sign: An itchy, raised rash, or puffy eyes or lips, while breathing stays normal
allergic.why: Your body may be reacting to the product, and using it again can bring the reaction back.

cardiovascular.sign: Pain, pressure or tightness in the chest, or pain that spreads to the arm, neck, jaw or back
cardiovascular.why: This can be a heart attack, which needs treatment in hospital straight away.

cardiovascular.sign: Sudden, severe shortness of breath: gasping, or not able to finish a sentence
cardiovascular.why: This can be a serious problem with the heart, the lungs or an allergic reaction.

cardiovascular.sign: A racing, pounding or irregular heartbeat that does not settle, or that comes with chest pain, breathlessness or fainting
cardiovascular.why: This can be a dangerous heart rhythm.

cardiovascular.sign: A sudden, severe headache with blurred vision, chest pain, confusion or vomiting
cardiovascular.why: Blood pressure may be dangerously high, which can damage the brain, heart, kidneys and eyes.

cardiovascular.sign: An erection that lasts more than 3 hours, or a painful erection that will not go down
cardiovascular.why: Blood trapped in the penis can damage it for good if it is not treated quickly.

cardiovascular.sign: Palpitations that keep coming back, even if they pass and you then feel well
cardiovascular.why: A doctor can check whether your heart rhythm is normal.

metabolic.sign: Shaking, sweating or sudden hunger that turns into confusion or drowsiness
metabolic.why: Very low blood sugar can cause a fit or loss of consciousness; take something sugary if you can still swallow safely.

metabolic.sign: Severe, constant pain in the upper belly that spreads to the back, often with vomiting
metabolic.why: This can be an inflamed pancreas (pancreatitis), a known risk of GLP-1 medicines such as semaglutide and tirzepatide.

metabolic.sign: Vomiting so often that you cannot keep fluids down, or passing very little urine
metabolic.why: Losing too much fluid can damage the kidneys.

metabolic.sign: Yellow skin, or yellow whites of the eyes
metabolic.why: This can be a sign of a liver problem, gallstones or an inflamed pancreas.

metabolic.sign: Dark, red or cola-coloured urine together with muscle pain, tenderness or weakness
metabolic.why: Damaged muscle can release a protein that harms the kidneys (rhabdomyolysis).

neurological.sign: Sudden weakness or numbness on one side, a drooping face, or slurred or confused speech
neurological.why: These are signs of a stroke, which needs treatment in hospital straight away, even if the signs pass.

neurological.sign: A headache that starts suddenly and is extremely painful, or a headache with a stiff neck, confusion or a fit
neurological.why: This can be a stroke or another emergency in the brain.

neurological.sign: Sudden loss of sight in one or both eyes
neurological.why: This can be a stroke or damage to the nerve of the eye, and sight can be lost for good.

neurological.sign: A fit (seizure): jerking movements, or suddenly not responding
neurological.why: A fit can be caused by very low blood sugar or a problem in the brain, and needs checks straight away.
